finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the boolean result, so the admin check is never enforced. Any request that reaches the handler can run purgeAll(), including from a user without the admin permission.
finding.source: Any authenticated (or any request-context) user lacking the 'admin' permission sends a request to the purge endpoint.
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive purge operation.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) loads the user from the request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns false for a non-admin, but the result is ignored and there is no early return or error response

finding.guards_checked: There is no conditional on checkPerm's return value. Unlike rotateKeys (handlers.go:33), which uses mustPerm and returns on failure, purge has no guard. I found no middleware in this directory, which contains only handlers.go. Any upstream router-level admin check would be outside the code I could see.

verdict.guard_found: none (checkPerm at handlers.go:12 returns a bool that is discarded at :26; no early return; no middleware in the directory)
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm(u,"admin") as a bare statement, discarding its bool (defined at handlers.go:12-14), so purgeAll() at :27 runs for any user, unlike rotateKeys at :33 which returns on mustPerm failure.

verdict_facts.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm (a bool-returning function, defined at handlers.go:12-14) as a bare statement and discards the result, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any user who reaches the handler, unlike rotateKeys, which tests mustPerm at handlers.go:33.
